Order 
This writ petition has been filed seeking a mandamus, forbearing the respondents from reverting the petitioners from the post of Designated Officer in the name of repatriation to former service in violation of condition of service of the petitioners and consequently directing the respondents to pass orders for fixation of pay of the petitioners in the post of Designated Officer in the scale of pay of Rs.15600-39100+5700 GP as sanctioned in G.O.Ms.No.347 Health and Family Welfare (AB2)
Department dated 22.12.2011 from the date of their initial appointment, on permanent absorption of petitioners in the post of Designated Officer in Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drugs Administration Department with all consequential and other attendant benefits, within a time frame to be fixed by this Hon'ble Court.

2. Mr.A.L.Somayaji, learned senior counsel for the petitioners, in support of the twin prayer,
submitted that after the petitioners were appointed as Health Officers in the Tamil Nadu Public Health Department, they were further appointed as Designated Officers in the Food Safety and Standards Department under Section 36 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 on complete diversion from the Department of Public Health and Preventive Medicine.

entities.text: Department of Public Health and Preventive Medicine
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: After appointing them as Designated Officers, they are entitled to get the scale of pay of Rs.15600-39100+5700 GP.
But the said scale of pay has not been given to them.
Therefore, a representation has been given.
Pursuant thereto, the Commissioner of Food Safety and Drug Administration, in his letter dated 21.11.2014,
addressing
to the Secretary to Government, Health and Family Welfare Department, Chennai, has requested to fix their pay to the post of Designated Officer.

Now that the proposal is pending, there is an apprehension on the part of the petitioners that they may be sent back to the parent department as Health Officers in the Tamil Nadu Public Health Department, which cannot be done.

3. But this Court is unable to consider the first plea seeking to injunct the respondents from disturbing the petitioners in the post of Designated Officer by repatriating them to the former service as Health Officers under the Tamil Nadu Public Health Department, in violation of the service rules.

The reason is that the petitioners, while serving as Health Officers in the Tamil Nadu Public Health Department, no doubt, were appointed as Designated Officers under Section 36 of the Food Safety and Standards Act on complete diversion.
But the orders of posting them as Designated Officers do not say that they would be permanently retained.
When this Court is not able to find any semblance of apprehension, it is too early for the petitioners to ask for the relief of injunction.
Accordingly, the said prayer is refused.

sentences.text: However, with regard to the second plea that the petitioners are not paid with the salary to the post of Designated Officer, in spite of the proposal sent by the Commissioner of Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration to the Secretary to Government, Health and Family Welfare Department dated 21.11.2014, the respondents are directed to consider the aforesaid proposal and pass appropriate orders with regard to the payment of salary to the post of Designated Officer from the date of appointment to the petitioners, in accordance with law.
With this observation, the writ petition stands disposed of.
Consequently, W.M.P.Nos.35105 to 35107 of 2017 are closed.
No costs.
